sources.title: Google SRE Book: Service Level Objectives
sources.claim_checked: Defines SLI/SLO/SLA, user-facing measurement, request latency/error rate/throughput and aggregation concepts.
supports: SLI is a carefully defined quantitative measure
SLO is a target measured by SLI
request-based SLI should be defined by user-relevant behavior
sources.limitations: The chapter provides principles and examples, not a service-specific SLO design.

sources.title: Google SRE Book: Availability Table
sources.claim_checked: The table shows 99.9% as 43.2 minutes per month under time-based unavailable-duration accounting; text distinguishes aggregate operation failures.
sources.limitations: The 43.2 minute figure is a time-window conversion and does not translate a request-count error budget to downtime.

sources.title: Prometheus Overview
sources.claim_checked: Prometheus stores labeled time series and primarily collects via HTTP pull scrapes; architecture includes server, scrape targets and optional ecosystem components.
supports: Prometheus overview and pull scrape model
sources.limitations: Conceptual overview; does not establish health of a particular application or complete business transaction.

sources.title: Prometheus Jobs and Instances
sources.claim_checked: `up{job,instance}` is 1 when instance is reachable/healthy for scrape and 0 when scrape failed; lists scrape-specific metrics.
supports: up is not an end-user business success SLI
sources.limitations: `healthy` here is the target scrape perspective, not semantic application correctness; another job/target requires its own series.

sources.title: Prometheus HTTP API
sources.claim_checked: Documents `/api/v1/query`, `/api/v1/query_range`, and `/api/v1/targets` target-discovery state, active/dropped targets, labels, health and scrape details.
sources.limitations: Documentation inspected only; no local or remote Prometheus API was called. `/ready` was not confirmed.

sources.title: Prometheus Configuration
sources.claim_checked: Config file flag and scrape interval/timeout settings; scrape_timeout cannot exceed scrape_interval.
sources.limitations: No verified statement found for subsecond intervals/timeouts.

sources.title: Prometheus Command Line Reference
sources.claim_checked: Documents `--web.listen-address` default `0.0.0.0:9090`, `--config.file`, and TSDB path flags.
sources.limitations: Does not establish whether port `0` is accepted for ephemeral binding or what port is then discoverable.

sources.title: Prometheus Metric and Label Naming
sources.claim_checked: Each unique label combination creates a time series; high-cardinality user IDs/emails/unbounded dimensions are discouraged; include unit/type in names.
sources.limitations: Guidance rather than a hard runtime prohibition.

sources.title: Prometheus Query Functions
sources.claim_checked: `rate()` computes average per-second increase, adjusts counter resets, extrapolates to range bounds; apply before aggregation. `histogram_quantile()` interpolates bucket values.
sources.limitations: Quantile accuracy depends on histogram buckets and assumptions; it is not an exact percentile over retained individual observations.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry Signals
sources.claim_checked: Defines telemetry signal families, including traces, metrics and logs.
sources.limitations: Signal terminology alone does not mean an application is instrumented or exporting telemetry.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry Traces
sources.claim_checked: Spans describe operations; context propagation correlates spans across services into a trace; exporters send trace data to consumers.
sources.limitations: A correlation ID appearing in logs alone does not establish OTel spans, propagation, or an exported trace.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry Trace SDK: Sampling
sources.claim_checked: Sampling controls telemetry noise/overhead by reducing collected/sent traces; SDK and downstream stages may sample.
sources.limitations: Exact sampling policy is implementation-specific; sampled traces are not guaranteed complete.

sources.title: W3C Trace Context
sources.claim_checked: Defines `traceparent` and optional `tracestate` propagation fields for interoperable trace context.
sources.limitations: Propagation format is not itself proof that spans were created, sampled, exported, or stored.

sources.title: Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaling
sources.claim_checked: Controller sync period default 15s, configurable; CPU initialization period defaults 5m and readiness state affects which samples are considered.
sources.limitations: Controller cadence is not end-to-end scale completion time; actual behavior depends on metrics, workloads, capacity and dependencies.

sources.title: Amazon CloudFront: Understand the Cache Key
sources.claim_checked: Cache key determines hits; response-varying request values belong in cache key; default key includes distribution domain and path; policy can vary on headers/cookies/query strings.
supports: cache key and personalized response safety
sources.limitations: Specific CloudFront behavior; cache policy and origin response controls must be examined for a concrete distribution.

sources.title: Google SRE Workbook: Alerting on SLOs
sources.claim_checked: Defines burn rate relative to SLO error-budget consumption, derives alert behavior from window and budget spend, and notes low-traffic difficulties.
sources.limitations: Examples illustrate tradeoffs and should not be copied without workload-specific traffic and response requirements.

sources.title: Google SRE Workbook: Postmortem Culture
sources.claim_checked: Recommends blameless review, learning, and actionable follow-up to reduce recurrence.
sources.limitations: Organizational practice; does not imply that a particular team performed a postmortem.

sources.title: AWS Well-Architected Reliability Pillar: Plan for Disaster Recovery
sources.claim_checked: RTO/RPO should follow business requirements; availability and DR have different scopes; DR implementation should be tested.
sources.limitations: Cloud-provider guidance; does not establish actual recovery performance in this environment.

sources.title: AWS Well-Architected Reliability Pillar: Back Up Data
sources.claim_checked: Backups should meet RTO/RPO requirements and periodic recovery should verify integrity and process.
sources.limitations: Recommendation, not evidence of any particular backup or restore test.

sources.title: Python 3.14 sqlite3 Documentation
sources.claim_checked: Documents SQLite connection backup API for copying a database to another connection.
sources.limitations: Local database API semantics do not demonstrate production RPO/RTO, backup isolation, restore operations, or service recovery.
